rules.title: California Civil Rights Council regulations on criminal history in housing decisions
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but with strict limits on what type of criminal history may be sought, how it may be considered, and what actions may be taken based on it. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.key_value: Blanket bans on applicants with criminal records prohibited; arrests without convictions may not be considered; effective Jan. 1, 2020

coverage.summary: Applies to criminal history use in housing decisions; the document states no unit-count or building-age limits.

rules.effective_date_note: Regulations adopted in 2019 by the California Civil Rights Council (formerly the Fair Employment and Housing Council); took effect Jan. 1, 2020.

rules.title: SB 329: source of income includes government housing subsidies (FEHA)
rules.requirement: The FEHA definition of source of income includes government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8, so landlords may not refuse to participate in such programs ("No Section 8" policies are unlawful).
rules.key_value: Effective Jan. 1, 2020; CRD enforcement lawsuits against violators

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords generally; the document states no size or age limits.

rules.quoted_span: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.
rules.review_note: Secondary source; codified sections in aliases are not stated in the document and should be verified.

rules.title: SB 267: credit history use for applicants with government rental subsidy (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Rental property owners may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy such as Section 8 as part of the application process without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.key_value: Must offer alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent

coverage.summary: Applies to applicants with a government rental subsidy.
coverage.other_conditions: Applicant must have a government rental subsidy such as Section 8.

rules.effective_date_note: Document says only that SB 267 was enacted 'last year' without a date; the article's own publication date is not given.

rules.quoted_span: last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
